# Playbook for hx_picket_nerfed

**On hiding:** Position yourself in the center of the range (4-6) early in the game to balance your offensive and defensive posture. In later rounds, shift away from central positions to avoid predictable targeting patterns that stronger competitors might exploit. When leading significantly in the final round, move to an edge or near-edge position (1-3 or 7-9) to minimize the probability of being hit by boats searching the center.

**On notes:** Post a cooperative opening message in round 1 to establish baseline trust and signal openness to coordination. As the game progresses, match the tone of the patrol—when others signal stability with "steady on station," echo that signal to maintain social cohesion and avoid escalating tension. Continue this pattern even in final rounds to avoid signaling desperation or triggering aggressive responses.

**On firing:** Follow the standing order without deviation. The standing order exists to coordinate fire patterns across the picket. When executing the standing order, choose your fire cell based on pattern-breaking logic: if you've fired the same cell before, use a different one; if firing at the same target repeatedly, vary your cell selection to avoid being predicted. Accept that variability will produce misses—this is preferable to establishing a predictable firing pattern that opponents can exploit.

**On claims:** Always claim truthfully what the office tells you. Do not lie about shot results, even in final rounds. Provable dishonesty breaks the game's information integrity and risks penalties you cannot see coming. Truth-telling is not optional even when behind or desperate.

**On escorts:** Before the escort stage, identify which boat has been least aggressive toward you or most aligned with your interests. Claim to escort that boat in hopes of a mutual 5-point exchange. If you have no clear preference or cannot identify a reliable candidate, claim none rather than guessing randomly. A failed escort claim yields 0 points; a random guess risks embarrassment and wastes a decision.

**On threat assessment:** Track each boat's score and hit count against you separately. Prioritize defense against boats that have hit you multiple times, not just boats with high total scores. A boat with 10 points that hit you once is less urgent than a boat with 6 points that hit you twice.

**On Harbor:** Never fire on Harbor. The payroll jettison rule makes Harbor a poor target—you gain only 3 points while breaking the standing order, and Harbor's threat to put you off the board is credible and costly. Respect the standing order around Harbor and focus fire on the rotation of Echo-Foxtrot-Gamma.

**On winning:** Do not assume a lead is safe until the game ends. Maintain discipline and follow your playbook throughout all rounds, including when ahead. Defensive positioning in the final round is more important than aggressive play. A lead is only secure after salvage claims resolve; play for confirmed victory, not expected victory.

# My Sonar Picket Playbook

## Hiding

When choosing a hide position, avoid the center (5) as a default—it's too obvious and gets fired at repeatedly. Vary between off-center positions (3, 4, 6, 7) to stay unpredictable. Don't repeat the same position in consecutive rounds.

When a shooter has hit me recently, move away from that cell immediately. When multiple shooters are targeting me, spread my movements widely rather than adjusting by one or two cells.

Track which boats are shooting at me consistently. If Echo has hit me in rounds 3 and 4, moving to position 2 in round 6 may not be enough—I need to understand Echo's targeting pattern and predict where they'll look in the final round.

## Firing

When firing at my standing order target, choose fire positions based on what I know about that target's recent movements, not arbitrary values. If a target has been hiding in a narrow range, fire within that range. If they're unpredictable, fire in the middle of the board (4-6) rather than extremes.

Don't assume extreme fire values (1, 9) are strong just because they're maximally different from recent shots. Fire where the target is likely to be.

After multiple misses against the same target, don't assume my statistical reasoning about "likely positions" is working. Consider that my target may be actively avoiding my predicted zones. Against unpredictable opponents, I may need to pick a position and commit to pattern-breaking rather than optimizing based on incomplete information.

## Claiming

When I get a private result from the office, I must claim honestly. The rules require my public claim to match the private result I was told—this is non-negotiable, not a strategic choice.

Don't rationalize false claiming as uncertainty-creation. The game mechanics prevent this; my claim must match the office's result or I violate the rules.

## Escort Claims

When no mutual escort relationship is obvious or established, claim none. Don't randomly name other boats hoping for the 5-point mutual bonus—this wastes my action unless I've coordinated with another boat.

When I can identify a boat that might escort me back (through notes or patterns), name that boat, but only if it seems genuinely likely they'll reciprocate.

## Station Notes

Use notes to signal stability or consistency when appropriate, but don't rely on notes for strategy. They're mostly for flavor and won't change outcomes.

Consistent notes ("steady on station" every round) may actually make me more vulnerable if my hiding is inconsistent, because boats may interpret my calm signals as permission to lock onto a position and fire strategically.

## Overall Strategy

I scored 2 points across 6 rounds by hitting once in round 1 and then missing repeatedly while being hit twice. The game is tighter than I thought. Early success (round 1 hit) matters, but I need to convert subsequent firing opportunities better.

Focus on surviving early and landing hits when I can. Don't get clever with false claims—that's not an option. But do pay attention to active shooter patterns: if a boat has hit me multiple times, I need to predict their next move more carefully, not just move randomly away from their last shot.

Escort claims require actual coordination, which I haven't attempted. In future games, explore whether establishing mutual escorts early could generate consistent bonus points to offset being hit.

# SONAR PICKET PLAYBOOK

## HIDING
When choosing where to hide, vary your position across rounds rather than anchoring on the same cell. Track which cells you've used and which cells the shooters targeting you have been firing at. Rotate through different regions (low, middle, high) unpredictably rather than staying central. If a shooter has demonstrated accuracy against you, move away from cells you've previously used. Mid-range cells (4-6) are solid opening positions when all shooters are unknown. After establishing a baseline, deliberately avoid repeating cells to stay unpredictable.

## NOTES
Post "steady on station" consistently unless you have a specific tactical reason to communicate something else. This establishes a baseline that makes any deviation meaningful if you need to signal later. Maintain consistency throughout all six rounds—deviating signals weakness or draws attention.

## FIRING
Follow standing orders unless Harbor jettison mechanics or strategic advantage clearly override them. When firing under standing orders, vary your target cell rather than repeating the same number. If you hit on one round, fire a different cell next time you target the same boat. When the target boat has moved predictably in response to previous fire, consider adjusting based on that pattern rather than random variation. On the final round, vary from cells you've already used against that target in this patrol.

## CLAIMING
Always claim truthfully what the office tells you. Never file a false claim. Honesty preserves your integrity in a multi-round competitive environment and prevents the game office from catching you in dishonesty, which would damage credibility.

## ESCORT CLAIMS
Before committing to an escort claim, determine which other boats have shown patterns suggesting they might name you back. Mutual escort claims are worth 5 points each. Track escort reciprocations across rounds. When you see another boat starting to establish an escort pattern with you, name them back to lock in the mutual bonus. Do not waste escort claims on boats that have not reciprocated before. On the final round, do not initiate new escort claims unless you have clear evidence of mutual intent from prior rounds. A single round of reciprocation is not enough—require sustained pattern evidence before claiming in round 6.

## GENERAL
Monitor your point lead carefully. When ahead, avoid unnecessary risks like Harbor jettison mechanics. Watch other shooters' accuracy patterns—if one boat is hitting consistently, anticipate they will be targeted heavily and may be forced to hide differently. Preserve ammunition efficiency by not overcommitting firepower early when the game runs multiple rounds. End the patrol with a clear record of tactical choices that position you well for future patrols: truthful claims, consistent notes, and disciplined escort claims build credibility for later games.
